claims.text: The memory sealing module is src/memory-seal.ts. It defines SEAL_FILE = ".seal.json" and sealPath() which resolves to memory/.seal.json under the agentik home.

checkSeal(file, content, home) in src/memory-seal.ts detects out-of-band modification: it compares the sha256 digest of the current content against the stored seal entry for that file's key; if no entry exists it accepts and seals silently ('unsealed'), if the digests match it returns 'sealed', and if they differ it returns 'diverged'.
DIVERGED_BODY constant defines the placeholder text shown for diverged files: "[BLOCKED: modified out of band — agentik memory reseal to accept]".

The initial identifier search for 'checkSeal(', 'DIVERGED', 'SealStatus', 'unsealFile(', 'sealFile(' returned zero hits across the repo, which is inconsistent with these identifiers being defined and exported in src/memory-seal.ts (confirmed via read_file). This discrepancy has not yet been resolved and call sites outside memory-seal.ts have not yet been located.
src/memory-seal.ts:26 — export const SEAL_FILE = ".seal.json"; this is the filename component of the seal path.

src/memory-seal.ts:35-37 — export function sealPath(home?: string): string returns join(memoryPaths(agentikHome(home)).memoryDir, SEAL_FILE), i.e. memory/.seal.json under the resolved agentik home's memory directory.

src/memory-seal.ts:57-63 — writeSeal(seal, home) is the low-level writer: it mkdir's the seal's directory, writes the JSON to a tmp file (`${path}.tmp-${pid}-${Date.now()}`), then renames it atomically over sealPath(home). This, combined with sealContent (66-72) and sealFile (75-88), is the module that writes memory/.seal.json — all three go through the module mutex `locked()` (28-33) so writes are serialized.

src/memory-seal.ts:66-72 — sealContent(key, content, home) computes digest(content) and stores it at seal[key], then calls writeSeal; used to seal in-memory content directly (e.g. after buildContext writes).

src/memory-seal.ts:75-88 — sealFile(file, home) seals a file as it exists on disk: if the file no longer exists it deletes the seal entry and returns "unsealed"; otherwise it reads the file, stores digest(content) under sealKey(file), writes the seal, and returns "sealed".

src/memory-seal.ts:102-115 — checkSeal(file, content, home) is the function that detects an out-of-band modification. It reads the current seal map, looks up have = seal[key] (the stored digest) and now = digest(content) (the recomputed digest of the content actually being used). If have === undefined (no prior seal entry) it accepts the content, seals it silently, and returns "unsealed" (line 108-111). Otherwise it returns "sealed" if have === now, else "diverged" (line 113) — a straight string-equality comparison of the two sha256 hex digests.
src/memory-seal.ts:24 — export type SealStatus = "sealed" | "unsealed" | "diverged" — the three possible return values of checkSeal/sealFile.

src/memory-seal.ts:117 — export const DIVERGED_BODY = "[BLOCKED: modified out of band — agentik memory reseal to accept]"; per the file's module doc-comment (lines 7-14) this text is what a caller substitutes for a memory file's body when checkSeal returns "diverged", until a human runs `agentik memory reseal`.
src/memory-seal.ts:44-46 — digest(content) is the hashing primitive both sealFile/sealContent (writers) and checkSeal (detector) use: createHash("sha256").update(content).digest("hex").

src/memory-seal.ts:7-18 (module doc-comment) — states this scheme is tamper-EVIDENT not tamper-proof (no HMAC, since a key would live in the same home as the files), so it catches accidental/unprivileged out-of-band writes, not a root-level attacker who could edit the seal file itself.
SEAL_FILE constant is ".seal.json"; sealPath(home) joins memoryPaths(agentikHome(home)).memoryDir with SEAL_FILE to produce memory/.seal.json
writeSeal performs an atomic write: writes JSON to a tmp file then renames it to sealPath(home)
sealContent(key, content, home?) records digest(content) under key in the seal map and persists via writeSeal — this along with sealFile is what writes memory/.seal.json
sealFile(file, home?) seals a file as currently on disk (digest of readFile), or deletes its seal entry if the file no longer exists

checkSeal(file, content, home?) is the function that detects an out-of-band modification: it compares the stored digest (have) to a freshly recomputed digest (now) of the given content; if no stored entry exists it seals silently and returns "unsealed"; if they match it returns "sealed"; if they differ it returns "diverged"
SealStatus is the type "sealed" | "unsealed" | "diverged"
DIVERGED_BODY is the exported constant string "[BLOCKED: modified out of band — agentik memory reseal to accept]", used as placeholder content when a caller detects a diverged seal

memory-seal.ts itself contains no refusal logic (no code path that aborts an operation) — checkSeal only returns a status; callers (e.g. memory-store.ts) are responsible for refusing writes/reads on "diverged", which is out of scope for this task

Seal file location constant: SEAL_FILE = ".seal.json" (src/memory-seal.ts:26), resolved to the full path memory/.seal.json by sealPath(home?) (src/memory-seal.ts:35-37), which joins memoryPaths(agentikHome(home)).memoryDir with SEAL_FILE.

The module that writes memory/.seal.json is src/memory-seal.ts itself. writeSeal(seal, home?) (src/memory-seal.ts:57-63) performs the actual atomic write: mkdir the parent dir, write JSON to a tmp file (`${path}.tmp-${pid}-${Date.now()}`), then rename() over sealPath(home). It is called by sealContent (src/memory-seal.ts:66-72, records a digest for one key) and sealFile (src/memory-seal.ts:75-88, seals a file as currently on disk, or deletes its entry if the file is absent) and by checkSeal itself when auto-sealing a first-seen file. All three go through locked() (src/memory-seal.ts:29-33), a module-level promise chain that serializes concurrent seal mutations.

The function that detects an out-of-band modification is checkSeal(file, content, home?) (src/memory-seal.ts:102-115). It reads the seal map, looks up the previously stored digest `have = seal[key]` (line 106) and computes `now = digest(content)` for the content being checked (line 107). If have === undefined (no prior entry), it treats the file as first-seen, writes `now` into the seal, and returns "unsealed" (lines 108-112) — this is a silent accept-and-seal path, not a divergence. Otherwise it returns "sealed" if have === now, else "diverged" (line 113): a stored sha256 digest (digest() at src/memory-seal.ts:44-46 = createHash("sha256").update(content).digest("hex")) that no longer matches the recomputed digest of the current on-disk content is the divergence signal.

SealStatus type = "sealed" | "unsealed" | "diverged" (src/memory-seal.ts:24). DIVERGED_BODY = "[BLOCKED: modified out of band — agentik memory reseal to accept]" (src/memory-seal.ts:117), the placeholder text a caller substitutes for real content when checkSeal returns "diverged".

checkSeal itself only returns a SealStatus; it does not refuse anything. Per the file's module docstring (src/memory-seal.ts:8-14, 20-21), refusal of writes/reads on a diverged seal is enforced by callers, not by memory-seal.ts. Two search_code queries for the string "memory-seal.ts" returned zero hits, so the import line in memory-store.ts (the expected entry point) could not be confirmed from within this task's allowed scope; identifying every operation that refuses on "diverged" is out of scope here per instructions (assigned to a caller-analysis task).
src/memory-seal.ts writes memory/.seal.json (SEAL_FILE = ".seal.json", path built by sealPath()); writeSeal()/sealContent()/sealFile() perform the writes, roughly lines 57-96 of the file.

checkSeal(file, content, home) in src/memory-seal.ts (~lines 102-115) is the function that detects an out-of-band modification: it compares a live content hash to the stored seal entry and returns "diverged" on mismatch.

memoryApply() in src/memory-store.ts refuses (returns ok:false with DIVERGED_MESSAGE) when readSealed(...).status === "diverged", before applying any add/replace/remove operation; memoryAdd, memoryReplace, and memoryRemove all call memoryApply and inherit this refusal.
memoryRemoveEntry() in src/memory-store.ts (backing `agentik memory remove`) performs the same diverged check and refuses before matching or removing an entry.

memorySnapshot() in src/memory-store.ts also checks the seal but does not refuse on divergence; it substitutes DIVERGED_BODY as the displayed content and logs an incident instead of rejecting the read.

No seal-check or refusal logic exists outside src/memory-seal.ts and src/memory-store.ts; src/cli.ts and src/loop.ts only call into memory-store.ts's gated functions, and src/backends.ts has no involvement with sealing.

taskResults.summary:
Investigation complete (search_code returned zero hits even for identifiers confirmed present in src/memory-seal.ts across 6 queries — the tool appears non-functional/misconfigured in this environment; I fell back to read_file, which does not annotate line numbers, so the line ranges below are best-effort estimates from sequential reading, not exact indexed positions).

Findings:
- Seal writer module: src/memory-seal.ts (whole file, ~117 lines). Writes memory/.seal.json via writeSeal()/sealContent()/sealFile() (~lines 57-96).
- Divergence detector: checkSeal(file, content, home) in src/memory-seal.ts, ~lines 102-115. Hashes live content and compares to the stored seal entry; returns "diverged" on mismatch, "unsealed" (and self-seals) if no entry exists, "sealed" if it matches.
- src/memory-store.ts wraps checkSeal in a private helper readSealed(target, home, workspace) (reads the file then calls checkSeal), used as the single choke point for every seal check in that file.
- Refusing operations (all in src/memory-store.ts, all gated by `readSealed(...).status === "diverged"`):
  1. memoryApply(target, ops, opts) — the central write path; returns `{ ok: false, message: DIVERGED_MESSAGE(...) }` without applying the op when diverged. memoryAdd, memoryReplace, memoryRemove (exported wrappers right after it) all funnel through memoryApply, so every add/replace/remove exposed via the CLI and the model's `memory` tool inherits the refusal.
  2. memoryRemoveEntry(target, needle, opts) — backs `agentik memory remove`; performs the same diverged check before matching/removing an entry and returns `{ ok: false, message: DIVERGED_MESSAGE(...), candidates: [] }`.
- Not a refusal (excluded per task scope): memorySnapshot also calls readSealed, but on divergence it does not refuse — it returns a snapshot whose body is replaced with DIVERGED_BODY ("[BLOCKED: modified out of band...]") and logs an incident; this is a display-time substitution, not a rejected operation.
- resealMemory
